To express the number in Cartesian form, we expand the parentheses and substitute the values of the cosine and sine.

Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =4(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =4(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\text{i}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =2\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{2}\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$
